ddl:
CREATE TABLE Student (
    Age INTEGER,
    Game_Preference VARCHAR(255),
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255),
    Student_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
);

CREATE TABLE Instructor (
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Instructor_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    Work_Duration VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Course (
    Course_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Course_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Credits FLOAT,
    Instructor_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Location VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Instructor_ID) REFERENCES Instructor(Instructor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Attendance_Record (
    Attendance_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Check-in_Time DATETIME,
    Class_Time DATETIME,
    Course_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Remarks VARCHAR(255),
    Student_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Student_ID, Course_ID, Check-in_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Course_ID) REFERENCES Course(Course_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Student_ID) REFERENCES Student(Student_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Leave_Record (
    Class_Time DATETIME,
    Course_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Leave_Reason VARCHAR(255),
    Leave_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Leave_Time DATETIME,
    Student_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Student_ID, Course_ID, Leave_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Course_ID) REFERENCES Course(Course_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Student_ID) REFERENCES Student(Student_ID)
);
gold_question: The system is a student attendance management system. In student management, the system maintains basic information for each student, including Student ID, name, age, phone number, game preference, and gender. In course management, the system records detailed information for each course, including Course ID, course name, location, credits, and instructor ID. In instructor management, the system maintains basic information for instructors, including Instructor ID, name, gender, title, and work duration. In attendance management, the system automatically records student attendance check-ins, including Student ID, Course ID, check-in time, attendance status, class time, and remarks, achieving automated attendance management. In leave management, the system tracks and records student leave requests, including Student ID, Course ID, leave time, class time, leave reason, and leave status, facilitating comprehensive management of student attendance by the school. The system achieves automated recording of student attendance, standardized management of leave requests, and unified maintenance of course and instructor information through the collaborative functioning of these functional modules.
nl_text:
The database schema named 'rschema_0444' contains five tables: Student, Instructor, Course, Attendance_Record, and Leave_Record.
The Student table represents a collection of students, with each student having an Age, Game_Preference, Gender, Name, Phone, and Student_ID. The Student_ID is the primary key of this table.
The Instructor table contains information about instructors, including Gender, Instructor_ID, Name, Title, and Work_Duration. The Instructor_ID is the primary key of this table.
The Course table contains details about the courses, including Course_ID, Course_Name, Credits, Instructor_ID, and Location. The Instructor_ID is a foreign key referencing the Instructor table, and Course_ID is the primary key of this table.
The Attendance_Record table records attendance information, including Attendance_Status, Check-in_Time, Class_Time, Course_ID, Remarks, and Student_ID. The combination of Student_ID and Course_ID, along with Check-in_Time, is the primary key of this table. Course_ID and Student_ID are foreign keys referencing the Course and Student tables respectively.
Finally, the Leave_Record table records information about student absences, including Class_Time, Course_ID, Leave_Reason, Leave_Status, Leave_Time, and Student_ID. The combination of Student_ID and Course_ID, along with Leave_Time, is the primary key of this table. Course_ID and Student_ID are foreign keys referencing the Course and Student tables respectively.
This schema ensures data integrity by enforcing primary and foreign key constraints, and it allows for referential integrity by maintaining the relationships between tables.
